items.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024
items.q: And she also had me play cymbals.

ctx.x: Oh six. I was wondering when you started — this is an assumption on my part — that you started fantasizing about this wonderful drumset, that if only I could have one.

Oh that was when I was in junior high school probably and got my first Gretsch catalogue. But I think the real genesis of the attraction was at Mrs. Rumbal’s nursery school in Tulsa, Oklahoma. And we had a marching band. And I was assigned what they called back then rhythm sticks. They were red of course, and were serrated so you could also make sounds by rubbing them like that. And she also had me play cymbals. And I still have one of the cymbals, it’s a little tiny cymbal about that big with a big wooden knob…

jazz players in Tulsa at the time. And he would take me to some of their gigs and I’d listen to that and then on a number of occasions we’d go to an African-American church and listen to the music there. And we all know the kind of joyous sounds that come out of that. So that really, really enticed me as well.
